reason: B is the only candidate that validates the ordinary host before the port as R3 requires (A, C and D parse the port first), and C additionally mis-offsets IPv6 port errors and validates the fragment before userinfo/path.
A and B wrongly return UnsupportedOperator for other punctuation that R8 says must be InvalidName, and C accepts names starting with a digit, while D follows R8 and R10 exactly.
A reports an empty interior component at the byte before its terminating slash (/a//b gives 2 instead of 3), while B correctly matches all R4 offset examples and the rest of the spec.

All candidates appear to implement the same SCC, arc, priority-Kahn and lexicographic shortest-route semantics correctly; C uses an explicitly lexicographic distance-guided route reconstruction and is fully spec-consistent.

C rejects valid decimals such as -0.01, and A and B can panic on very long decimal integral parts during overflow computation, whereas D saturates and reports DecimalOverflow while matching the other requirements.

Only C lets the first alphabetic byte (including N/n) set the case and reports MixedCase at the first byte of the other case, whereas A and B skip N/n and D picks uppercase whenever any uppercase exists.

A fails to continue FIFO dispatch at the same tick after an inline zero-duration Finish (it can stop or jump ahead to the next arrival), while B dispatches waiting customers immediately as R13 requires.

C and D panic via expect when an eligible task exists but no worker is free, and A emits simultaneous end lines in descending task order with fragile index removal, whereas B handles all of these correctly.
